title.zh: 卷438 列傳二百二十五 阎敬铭 张之万 鹿傳霖 林绍年
title.en: Volume 438 Biographies 225: Yan Jingming, Zhang Zhiwan, Lu Chuan Lin, Lin Shaonian
title.raw: 卷438 列傳二百二十五 阎敬铭 张之万 鹿傳霖 林绍年

sentences.zh: 列傳二百二十五

translations.literal: Biographies 225
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 225

sentences.zh: 閻敬銘張之萬鹿傳霖林紹年

translations.literal: Yan Jingming, Zhang Zhiwan, Lu Chuanlin, Lin Shaonian
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jingming, Zhang Zhiwan, Lu Chuanlin, and Lin Shaonian

sentences.zh: 閻敬銘，字丹初，陝西朝邑人。

translations.literal: Yan Jingming, style name Danchu, was a native of Chaoyi in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jingming, whose style was Danchu, came from Chaoyi in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 道光二十五年進士，選庶吉士，散館改戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and after leaving the academy was made a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1845, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and on completing his academy term was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年，湖北巡撫胡林翼奏調赴鄂，總司糧台營務。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng, Hubei governor Hu Linyi memorialized to have him transferred to Hubei to take charge of grain transport and camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, Hubei governor Hu Linyi had him transferred to the province to oversee grain supply and military logistics.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，擢四品京堂。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to director, then to a fourth-rank official in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to director and was then promoted to a fourth-rank capital post.

sentences.zh: 林翼請病，复疏薦敬銘才，授湖北按察使。

translations.literal: When Linyi requested sick leave, he again memorialized recommending Jingming's talent and had him appointed Hubei provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Linyi went on sick leave, he again recommended Yan's abilities in a memorial, and Yan was appointed Hubei provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，嚴樹森繼為巡撫，亦推敬銘湖北賢能第一，署布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Yan Shusen succeeded as governor and also ranked Jingming first among Hubei's worthy officials, appointing him acting provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, when Yan Shusen became governor, he likewise rated Yan Jingming the foremost talent in Hubei and named him acting provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 以丁本生父憂歸，命治喪畢赴軍，未行，詔署山東鹽運使，擢署巡撫，疏乞終制，不許。

translations.literal: He returned home on mourning for his biological father; he was ordered to join the army after the mourning period ended, but before he departed he was ordered to act as Shandong salt transport commissioner and promoted to acting governor; he memorialized begging to complete mourning, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning for his father and was told to rejoin the army once the mourning period ended; before he could leave, he was ordered to serve as acting Shandong salt transport commissioner and then acting governor. He asked to be allowed to finish mourning, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 時山東教匪入新泰，捻、幅各匪犯鄒、曲阜，降眾竄陽穀、聊城。

translations.literal: At the time Shandong religious rebels entered Xintai; Nian and Fu bandits attacked Zou and Qufu; surrendered troops fled into Yanggu and Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: At that time religious rebels in Shandong entered Xintai, Nian and Fu bandits raided Zou and Qufu, and surrendered troops scattered into Yanggu and Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 敬銘既受任，檄總兵保德等進剿，而自督軍規淄川，克之。

translations.literal: Once Jingming took office, he issued orders to brigade-general Baode and others to advance in suppression, while he himself directed the army to invest Zichuan and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Yan took office, he ordered Brigade-General Baode and others to press the attack while he personally led troops to besiege Zichuan and took the city.

sentences.zh: 已革參將宋景詩引降眾屯東昌，复叛，飭按察使丁寶楨討之。

translations.literal: The dismissed vice commander Song Jingshi led surrendered troops to encamp at Dongchang and rebelled again; he ordered provincial judicial commissioner Ding Baozhen to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The dismissed vice commander Song Jingshi had led surrendered troops to camp at Dongchang and rebelled again; Yan ordered provincial judicial commissioner Ding Baozhen to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 景詩竄莘，敬銘檄軍防運河，令之曰：「使一匪潛渡者，殺無赦！

translations.literal: Jingshi fled to Shen; Jingming ordered the army to guard the Grand Canal and commanded: "If a single bandit slips across in secret, execute without mercy!
translations.idiomatic: Song fled to Shen county; Yan ordered troops to guard the Grand Canal and declared, "If even one bandit crosses in secret, execute without mercy!

sentences.zh: 」而自移軍博平。

translations.literal: " He himself moved the army to Boping.
translations.idiomatic: " He then shifted his own forces to Boping.

sentences.zh: 已而保德、寶楨連敗賊唐邑馬橋，克王家海，別軍克甘官屯，賊遁開州。

translations.literal: Before long Baode and Baozhen repeatedly defeated the bandits at Tangyi and Maqiao, captured Wangjiahai, another force captured Ganguantun, and the bandits fled to Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Baode and Ding Baozhen won successive victories over the rebels at Tangyi and Maqiao, took Wangjiahai, and another column captured Ganguantun, driving the rebels toward Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 事平，再請終制，仍不許。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he again requested to complete mourning; still not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, he again asked to complete mourning, but was again refused.

sentences.zh: 三年，服除，實授。

translations.literal: In the third year, mourning ended and he received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864, when his mourning ended, he received a regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 奏言抽調綠營兵練騎隊，朝旨允行，令即遣散募勇。

translations.literal: He memorialized proposing to draw Green Standard troops to train cavalry units; the court approved and ordered him immediately to disband recruited braves.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Green Standard troops should be drawn off to train cavalry; the court approved and ordered him to disband the recruited braves at once.

sentences.zh: 敬銘言：「東省變故頻仍，亂甫定，降眾未必革心。

translations.literal: Jingming said: "The eastern province has suffered repeated upheavals; rebellion has only just been settled, and surrendered troops may not yet have changed their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "Shandong has been shaken by repeated crises; the rebellion has only just ended, and the surrendered men may not yet be loyal.

sentences.zh: 綠營廢弛已久，驟裁勇易啟戎心。

translations.literal: The Green Standard army has long been neglected; abruptly cutting braves may easily stir military discontent.
translations.idiomatic: The Green Standard forces have long been neglected; to dismiss the braves all at once could easily provoke mutiny.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢為節嗇帑項浮詞遺後患。

translations.literal: Your servant dares not offer empty words of thrift in the treasury and leave trouble for later.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not offer empty talk of saving money and leave trouble for those who come after.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「兵之能強，端恃將領。

translations.literal: " He also said: "An army's strength depends entirely on its commanders.
translations.idiomatic: " He went on, "An army's strength depends entirely on its commanders.

sentences.zh: 將領之材，亦資汲引。

translations.literal: Commanders' talent also depends on being drawn up and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders' talent, too, depends on being discovered and promoted.

sentences.zh: 如胡林翼、曾國籓、左宗棠倡率鄉里，楚將之名遂著。

translations.literal: Such men as Hu Linyi, Zeng Guofan, and Zuo Zongtang led their home districts, and the fame of Chu generals then became prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Hu Linyi, Zeng Guofan, and Zuo Zongtang rallied their home regions, and the fame of Hunan generals spread accordingly.

sentences.zh: 前者僧格林沁奏稱不宜專用南勇，啟輕視朝廷之漸。

translations.literal: Earlier Senggelinqin memorialized that southern braves should not be relied on exclusively, lest a tendency to slight the court arise.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sengge Rinchen had memorialized that the court should not rely solely on southern braves, lest contempt for the throne take root.

sentences.zh: 老成謀國，瞻言百里。

translations.literal: A seasoned statesman's counsel for the realm looks a hundred li ahead.
translations.idiomatic: That was the far-sighted counsel of a seasoned statesman.

sentences.zh: 自古名將，北人為多。

translations.literal: From antiquity famous generals have mostly been northerners.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout history, famous generals have mostly come from the north.

sentences.zh: 臣北人也，恥不知兵。

translations.literal: Your servant is a northerner and is ashamed not to understand warfare.
translations.idiomatic: I am a northerner myself, and I am ashamed not to understand warfare.

sentences.zh: 以在軍久，見諸軍之成敗利鈍，必求其所以然之故。

translations.literal: Having long been in the army, I have seen armies' victories, defeats, gains, and losses, and always sought the reasons why.
translations.idiomatic: Having long served with the armies, I have watched their victories and defeats and always sought the reasons behind them.

sentences.zh: 深知不求將而言兵，有兵與無兵等。

translations.literal: I deeply know that to speak of troops without seeking commanders is the same as having troops and not having them.
translations.idiomatic: I know well that to discuss armies without first securing commanders is no different from having no army at all.

sentences.zh: 今北方雖所在募勇，皆烏合耳。

translations.literal: Now although braves are recruited everywhere in the north, they are all mere rabble.
translations.idiomatic: Today, although braves are recruited everywhere in the north, they are only rabble.

sentences.zh: 為將者貪婪欺飾，不知尊君親上為何事，使握兵符，民變兵譁，後患滋大。

translations.literal: Those who serve as commanders are greedy and deceitful, do not know what it means to honor the ruler and revere superiors; if given military seals, popular uprisings and troop mutinies will follow and later troubles will grow.
translations.idiomatic: Their commanders are greedy and deceitful and do not know what it means to honor the throne; put arms in their hands and you invite popular revolt and mutiny, with worse trouble to follow.

sentences.zh: 故欲強兵必先儲將。

translations.literal: Therefore to strengthen troops one must first stock commanders.
translations.idiomatic: To build a strong army, one must first cultivate commanders.

sentences.zh: 北人之智勇兼備者，推多隆阿。

translations.literal: Among northerners who combine wisdom and courage, Duolong'a is foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Among northerners who combine wisdom and courage, Duolong'a stands foremost.

sentences.zh: 請飭多隆阿募北方將士，教之戰陣，擇其忠勇者，補授提、鎮、參、遊，俾綠營均成勁旅，何必更募勇丁？

translations.literal: I beg that Duolong'a be ordered to recruit northern officers and soldiers, teach them battle formations, select the loyal and brave among them, and appoint them as provincial commanders, brigade commanders, regimental commanders, and battalion commanders, so that Green Standard forces all become crack troops—why must more braves be recruited?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Duolong'a be ordered to recruit northern officers and soldiers, train them in warfare, and promote the loyal and brave among them to provincial, brigade, regimental, and battalion commands, so that the Green Standard armies become elite forces. Why recruit more braves?

sentences.zh: 」時捻患熾，台臣議行團練。

translations.literal: " At the time the Nian threat was fierce and censorial officials proposed instituting local militia training.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the Nian rebellion was raging, and censorial officials proposed organizing local militia.

sentences.zh: 敬銘言：「斂鄉里之財以為餉，集耕種之民以為兵，於事有害無益，不如力行堅壁清野之法。

translations.literal: Jingming said: "Gathering local wealth for pay and assembling farming people as soldiers harms affairs without benefit; it is better to enforce firmly the method of strengthening walls and clearing the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Yan objected: "To levy local wealth for pay and turn farmers into soldiers does more harm than good. It is better to enforce the policy of strengthening walls and clearing the countryside.

sentences.zh: 」事遂寢。

translations.literal: " The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 四年，僧格林沁戰歿曹州，賊勢張，益趨張秋南，將犯省城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Senggelinqin died in battle at Caozhou; the bandits' power swelled and they pressed further south toward Zhangqiu, about to attack the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865, Sengge Rinchen was killed in battle at Caozhou; the rebels grew bolder and pushed south toward Zhangqiu, threatening the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 敬銘督師東昌，還軍御之，增設砲劃防河，賊折而東。

translations.literal: Jingming directed troops at Dongchang, returned the army to resist them, added artillery and planned river defense, and the bandits turned east.
translations.idiomatic: Yan commanded at Dongchang, brought his army back to meet them, strengthened artillery defenses along the river, and the rebels turned east.

sentences.zh: 移軍兗州，賊竄豐、沛。

translations.literal: He moved the army to Yanzhou; the bandits fled to Feng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted his army to Yanzhou while the rebels fled toward Feng and Pei.

sentences.zh: 乃檄總兵楊飛熊間道趨滕，防賊還竄。

translations.literal: He then ordered brigade-general Yang Feixiong by a side route to hurry to Teng, to guard against the bandits doubling back.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Brigade-General Yang Feixiong by a side route to Teng to block any rebel attempt to double back.

sentences.zh: 賊果入湖濱，以飛熊扼運河，不得逞，竄徐州。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed entered the lakeshore region; Feixiong held the Grand Canal so they could not prevail and they fled to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did enter the lake district, but Yang held the Grand Canal and blocked their advance, forcing them toward Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊入鉅野，游擊王心安失利。

translations.literal: The next year the bandits entered Juye; battalion commander Wang Xin'an suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the rebels entered Juye, and Battalion Commander Wang Xin'an was defeated.

sentences.zh: 敬銘方臥疾，強起視師東平。

translations.literal: Jingming was then bedridden with illness but forced himself up to inspect the army at Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was ill in bed but roused himself to take command at Dongping.

sentences.zh: 兗沂曹濟道文彬督團勇擊賊，賊引去。

translations.literal: Circuit intendant Wen Bin of Yan-Yi-Cao-Ji directed militia to attack the bandits, and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit Intendant Wen Bin of Yan-Yi-Cao-Ji led militia against the rebels and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 敬銘赴濟寧，會曾國籓商定分扼黃、運之議。

translations.literal: Jingming went to Jining and met Zeng Guofan to agree on a plan to divide control of the Yellow River and the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Yan went to Jining and met Zeng Guofan to agree on how to divide control of the Yellow River and the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 賊復大股趨鉅野、金鄉，分擾運西。

translations.literal: The bandits again advanced in large bodies toward Juye and Jinxiang and raided west of the canal in separate bands.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels again advanced in force toward Juye and Jinxiang and raided the west bank of the canal in separate columns.

sentences.zh: 遣知府王成謙等要擊，而自督軍巡河，露宿四晝夜，賊連敗，始西遁。

translations.literal: He sent prefect Wang Chengqian and others to intercept; he himself directed the army patrolling the river, bivouacking in the open four days and nights; the bandits were repeatedly defeated and at last fled west.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Prefect Wang Chengqian and others to intercept them while he personally patrolled the river, sleeping in the open for four days and nights until the rebels were beaten repeatedly and fled west.

sentences.zh: 有張積中者，結寨肥城黃崖，集眾自保，以不受撫，夷之。

translations.literal: There was one Zhang Jizhong who fortified a stockade at Huangya in Feicheng, gathered a crowd for self-defense, and because he would not accept pacification was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zhang Jizhong had fortified Huangya in Feicheng and gathered followers for self-defense; because he refused to submit, Yan destroyed the stronghold.

sentences.zh: 六年，移疾歸，居久之，以工部侍郎召，不起。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home; after living there a long time he was summoned as vice minister of Works but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he resigned on grounds of illness and went home; long afterward he was summoned as vice minister of Works but declined.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，山西大饑，奉命察視賑務。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu a great famine struck Shanxi; he was ordered to inspect relief affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1877, when Shanxi suffered a great famine, he was ordered to inspect relief work.

sentences.zh: 奏劾侵帑知州段鼎耀，置之法。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeaching prefect Duan Dingyao for embezzling relief funds and had him punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized against Prefect Duan Dingyao for embezzling relief funds and had him punished.

sentences.zh: 請裁減山、陝諸省差徭，並追彈尚書恩承、童華前奉使四川過境擾累狀，均下吏議。

translations.literal: He requested reduction of corvée levies in Shanxi, Shaanxi, and other provinces, and also pursued impeachment of ministers En Cheng and Tong Hua for earlier missions to Sichuan that harassed the regions they passed through; all were referred to judicial review.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to cut corvée levies in Shanxi, Shaanxi, and other provinces, and also pursued charges against Ministers En Cheng and Tong Hua for harassing the regions they passed through on earlier missions to Sichuan; all cases were referred for judicial review.

sentences.zh: 八年，起戶部尚書，甫視事，以廣東布政使姚覲元、荊宜施道董俊漢賄結前任司員骫法，咸劾罷之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was recalled as minister of Revenue; as soon as he took office, because Guangdong provincial treasurer Yao Jingyuan and Jing-Yi-Shi circuit intendant Dong Junhan had bribed former ministry officials and violated law, he impeached and dismissed them all.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 he was recalled as minister of Revenue, and as soon as he took office he impeached and dismissed Guangdong provincial treasurer Yao Jingyuan and Jing-Yi-Shi Circuit Intendant Dong Junhan for bribing former ministry officials and breaking the law.

sentences.zh: 兼署兵部。

translations.literal: He also served concurrently as acting minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as acting minister of War.

sentences.zh: 疏陳興辦新疆屯田。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth establishing garrison farms in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on establishing garrison farms in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 明年，充軍機大臣、總理衙門行走，晉協辦大學士。

translations.literal: The next year he served as Grand Councilor and attendant at the Zongli Yamen, and was promoted to associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became a Grand Councilor and attendant at the Zongli Yamen and was promoted to associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授東閣大學士，仍筦戶部，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, still managing the Ministry of Revenue, and was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion while continuing to head the Ministry of Revenue, and was granted a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 自陳衰老，辭軍機大臣。

translations.literal: He stated himself old and declined the Grand Council post.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded old age and resigned from the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 時上意將修圓明園，而敬銘論治以節用為本，會廷議錢法，失太后旨，因革職留任。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor intended to restore the Old Summer Palace, while Jingming's theory of governance took thrift as fundamental; when the court debated currency policy he lost the empress dowager's favor and was therefore dismissed from office but retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: The court then intended to restore the Old Summer Palace, while Yan's governing principle was frugality; when the court debated currency reform he offended the empress dowager and was stripped of rank but kept in office.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復職，遂乞休，章四上，乃得請。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year his rank was restored; he then begged retirement, memorialized four times, and only then was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1887 his rank was restored, but he then asked to retire; only after four memorials was he allowed to leave office.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒，贈太子少保，諡文介。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died; he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1892 and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 敬銘質樸，以潔廉自矯厲，雖貴，望之若老儒。

translations.literal: Jingming was plain and unadorned, disciplined himself with purity and integrity; though honored in rank, in appearance he seemed an old scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was plain and unadorned and held himself to strict integrity; even at the height of rank he looked like an elderly scholar.

sentences.zh: 善理財，在鄂治軍需，足食足兵，佐平大難。

translations.literal: He was skilled at managing finances; in Hubei he managed military supplies, ensuring full provisions and full troops, and helped settle the great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at finance; in Hubei he managed military supplies so that armies were fed and equipped, helping to end the great rebellion.

sentences.zh: 及長戶部，精校財賦，立科條，令出期必行。

translations.literal: When he headed the Ministry of Revenue he carefully audited revenues and expenditures, established regulations, and orders issued on schedule were invariably carried out.
translations.idiomatic: As head of the Ministry of Revenue he audited finances carefully, set regulations, and saw that every order issued on schedule was carried out.

sentences.zh: 初直樞廷，太后頗信仗之，終以戇直早退雲。

translations.literal: When he first served in the Grand Council the empress dowager greatly trusted and relied on him, but in the end because of his blunt integrity he retired early.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered the Grand Council the empress dowager trusted him greatly, but in the end his blunt integrity brought an early retirement.

sentences.zh: 張之萬，字子青，直隸南皮人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhiwan, style name Ziqing, was a native of Nanpi in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiwan, whose style was Ziqing, came from Nanpi in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年，以一甲一名進士授修撰。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, as top graduate of the first class of jinshi he was appointed Hanlin compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1847, as top graduate of the jinshi examination, he was appointed Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，出督河南學政。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he went out as educational commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he was sent out as educational commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 粵賊破歸德，近偪開封，之萬條上防剿事宜，多允行。

translations.literal: Cantonese rebels captured Guide and approached Kaifeng; Zhiwan submitted detailed plans for defense and suppression, most of which were approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping rebels took Guide and threatened Kaifeng, Zhang submitted detailed plans for defense and suppression, most of which the court approved.

sentences.zh: 俄，召還，授鍾郡王讀。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled and appointed tutor to Prince Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to serve as tutor to Prince Zhong.

sentences.zh: 由侍讀累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: From reader in waiting he was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from reader in waiting to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢禮部侍郎，兼署工部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to vice minister of Rites and concurrently served as acting minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was promoted to vice minister of Rites and concurrently served as acting minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 嘗被詔偕太常寺卿許彭壽等匯輯前代帝王及垂簾事蹟可法戒者上之，錫名治平寶鑑。

translations.literal: He was once ordered together with Taichang Temple director Xu Pengshou and others to compile precedents from past dynasties' emperors and regencies that could serve as models or warnings and present them; it was granted the title Precious Mirror of Good Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was once ordered, together with Taichang Temple Director Xu Pengshou and others, to compile precedents from past emperors and regencies that could serve as models or warnings; the work was titled Precious Mirror of Good Governance.

sentences.zh: 會河南州縣以苛派擅殺為御史劉毓楠奏劾，命之萬往按，得實，巡撫鄭元善以下降黜有差，即以之萬署巡撫事。

translations.literal: When Henan prefectures and counties were impeached by censor Liu Yunan for harsh levies and unauthorized executions, Zhiwan was ordered to investigate; the charges were substantiated, and governor Zheng Yuanshan and others were demoted or dismissed in varying degrees; Zhiwan was then appointed acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Liu Yunan impeached Henan officials for harsh levies and unauthorized executions, Zhang was sent to investigate, confirmed the charges, and had Governor Zheng Yuanshan and others demoted or dismissed; Zhang was then named acting governor.

sentences.zh: 疏陳軍興財匱，請仿湖北變通漕折，言：「汴漕一石舊折銀四兩，今請令州縣留辦公費七錢，實解司庫三兩三錢，以二兩購米實倉，餘一兩充汴餉，其三錢為通省公費。

translations.literal: He memorialized that with military campaigns finances were exhausted and requested following Hubei's flexible grain-tax conversion, saying: "Bian grain transport formerly converted one shi to four taels of silver; now I request that prefectures and counties retain seven qian for office expenses, actually remit three taels three qian to the provincial treasury, use two taels to buy rice for the granary, the remaining one tael for Bian pay, and the three qian as general provincial expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that wartime finances were exhausted and asked to follow Hubei's flexible grain-tax conversion, proposing: "Bian grain transport formerly converted one shi to four taels of silver; now let prefectures and counties retain seven qian for office expenses, remit three taels three qian to the provincial treasury, use two taels to buy rice for the granary, devote one tael to Bian pay, and use the three qian as general provincial expenses.

sentences.zh: 」允行。

translations.literal: " This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 捻酋陳大喜犯南陽，之萬親赴汝州督師。

translations.literal: Nian chieftain Chen Daxi attacked Nanyang; Zhiwan personally went to Ruzhou to direct the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian chieftain Chen Daxi attacked Nanyang, Zhang went in person to Ruzhou to take command.

sentences.zh: 大喜竄阜陽，勾結皖捻，一由岳城趨楊莊偪雷堰，一入張岡，總兵張曜馳擊破之。

translations.literal: Daxi fled to Fuyang and colluded with Anhui Nian; one force by Yuecheng pressed toward Yangzhuang threatening Leiyan, another entered Zhanggang; brigade-general Zhang Yao rushed to attack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen fled to Fuyang and joined forces with Anhui Nian rebels; one column advanced from Yuecheng toward Yangzhuang to threaten Leiyan, another entered Zhanggang; Brigade-General Zhang Yao rushed to attack and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 團練大臣毛昶熙諸軍相繼至，連戰皆捷，斬逆酋張鳳舞，汝南肅清。

translations.literal: Militia commissioner Mao Changxi and other armies arrived in succession, winning every battle; the rebel chieftain Zhang Fengwu was beheaded and Runan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Militia Commissioner Mao Changxi and other forces arrived in succession and won every battle; rebel chieftain Zhang Fengwu was beheaded and Runan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 之萬駐軍許州，既分遣諸將設防，自引軍還省；

translations.literal: Zhiwan stationed the army at Xuzhou; after dispatching generals to set defenses, he himself led the army back to the provincial capital;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang stationed troops at Xuzhou, dispatched generals to set up defenses, and then led the main force back to the provincial capital;

sentences.zh: 而亳捻乘虛襲許，陷兩寨，坐降二級留任。

translations.literal: but Bozhou Nian took advantage to raid Xu, captured two stockades, and he was demoted two ranks but retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: but Bozhou Nian rebels seized the chance to raid Xuzhou and took two stockades, for which Zhang was demoted two ranks but kept in office.

sentences.zh: 西捻張總愚竄鄧州，藍大順走西坪，謀與合。

translations.literal: Western Nian leader Zhang Zongyu fled to Dengzhou; Lan Dashun went to Xiping, planning to join forces.
translations.idiomatic: Western Nian leader Zhang Zongyu fled to Dengzhou while Lan Dashun retreated to Xiping, intending to join forces.

sentences.zh: 張曜既敗總愚重陽店，乘勝襲西坪，大順亦敗走。

translations.literal: Zhang Yao had already defeated Zongyu at Chongyangdian, then pressed the victory to attack Xiping, and Dashun was also defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yao had already defeated Zhang Zongyu at Chongyangdian, then pressed the attack to Xiping and routed Lan Dashun as well.

sentences.zh: 之萬復進汝州。

translations.literal: Zhiwan again advanced to Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang again advanced to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，移屯南陽，賊犯開封，還軍擊走之。

translations.literal: In the third year he moved camp to Nanyang; when bandits attacked Kaifeng he returned the army and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he shifted camp to Nanyang; when rebels threatened Kaifeng he brought his army back and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷河道總督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to director-general of waterways.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he was transferred to director-general of waterways.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁戰歿曹州，督兵大臣皆獲咎。

translations.literal: Senggelinqin died in battle at Caozhou, and all military supervising grandees were blamed.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengge Rinchen was killed at Caozhou, every supervising commander was blamed.

sentences.zh: 之萬亦革職留任，以助防省城功，給二品頂戴。

translations.literal: Zhiwan too was dismissed from office but retained in post; for his merit in helping defend the provincial capital he was given a second-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang too was stripped of rank but kept in office; for helping defend the provincial capital he was given a second-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 五年，移督漕運。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to supervise grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he was transferred to supervise grain transport.

sentences.zh: 捻入徐州，之萬以里下河為財賦所出，嚴防清、淮及六塘河諸要地。

translations.literal: When Nian entered Xuzhou, Zhiwan, because the Lixiahe region was the source of revenue, strictly defended key points on the Qing and Huai rivers and the Liutang River.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian entered Xuzhou, Zhang, knowing the Lixiahe region was the province's fiscal heartland, strictly defended key points on the Qing and Huai rivers and the Liutang River.

sentences.zh: 六年，淮軍獲賴文光於揚州，東捻平。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Huai Army captured Lai Wenguang at Yangzhou and the eastern Nian were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 the Huai Army captured Lai Wenguang at Yangzhou and the eastern Nian rebellion ended.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，賜之萬花翎、頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: On news of victory he was granted a peacock feather and a first-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: On news of the victory he was granted a peacock feather and a first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 七年，會剿西捻，總愚溺死，東南大定。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he joined in suppressing the western Nian; Zongyu drowned and the southeast was greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he joined the campaign against the western Nian; Zhang Zongyu drowned and the southeast was finally pacified.

sentences.zh: 之萬疏陳江北善後事宜。

translations.literal: Zhiwan memorialized on postwar arrangements north of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang memorialized on postwar arrangements north of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 九年，調江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Jiangsu governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 he was transferred to governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 遷浙閩總督，以母老乞養歸。

translations.literal: He was moved to Zhe-Fujian governor-general, but because his mother was old begged to retire and return home to care for her.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor-general of Zhejiang and Fujian, but asked to retire and return home because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，起兵部尚書，調刑部。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu he was recalled as minister of War and transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 he was recalled as minister of War and then transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十年，入軍機，兼署吏部，充上書房總師傅、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he entered the Grand Council, concurrently served as acting minister of Personnel, and was appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study Hall and associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 he entered the Grand Council, concurrently served as acting minister of Personnel, and was appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study Hall and associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授體仁閣大學士，轉東閣。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence and transferred to the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1889 he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence and then transferred to the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 賜雙眼花翎、紫韁。

translations.literal: He was granted double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.

sentences.zh: 二十年，免直軍機。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was relieved of service in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 he was relieved of duty in the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 之萬入直凡十年，領樞密者為禮親王世鐸，治尚安靜，故得無事。

translations.literal: Zhiwan served in the council for ten years in all; the one who led state secrets was Prince Li Shiduo, whose governance favored quiet, and so affairs remained untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang served in the Grand Council for ten years altogether; Prince Li Shiduo led the council and favored a quiet approach to governance, so affairs remained largely untroubled.

sentences.zh: 及日韓事棘，之萬乃先罷退。

translations.literal: When the Japan-Korea crisis became acute, Zhiwan was the first to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japan-Korea crisis grew acute, Zhang was the first to step down.

sentences.zh: 又二年，以病致仕。

translations.literal: Two years later he retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十七，贈太傅，諡文達。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-seven, was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, and given the posthumous name Wenda.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-seven and was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Wenda.

sentences.zh: 鹿傳霖，字滋軒，直隸定興人。

translations.literal: Lu Chuanlin, style name Zixuan, was a native of Dingxing in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chuanlin, whose style was Zixuan, came from Dingxing in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 父丕宗，官都勻知府，死寇難，諡壯節，傳霖其第五子也。

translations.literal: His father Pizong served as prefect of Duyun and died in bandit calamity, posthumously named Zhuangjie; Chuanlin was his fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pizong had served as prefect of Duyun and died fighting bandits, receiving the posthumous name Zhuangjie; Chuanlin was his fifth son.

sentences.zh: 當丕宗守都勻時，叛苗麕聚城下，傳霖方率健卒迎餉，聞警，馳還助城守，相持十閱月，援絕城陷。

translations.literal: When Pizong was defending Duyun, rebellious Miao gathered below the city; Chuanlin was leading picked troops to meet supplies, heard the alarm, galloped back to help defend the city, held out ten months, relief was cut off and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: While Pizong was defending Duyun, rebel Miao gathered outside the walls; Chuanlin was leading picked troops to meet a supply convoy, but on hearing the alarm he galloped back to help defend the city. The siege lasted ten months until supplies were cut off and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 傳霖投總督告父死狀，大兵攻复都勻，奉父母遺骸歸葬，時年甫二十，由是知名。

translations.literal: Chuanlin went to the governor to report his father's death; the great army attacked and recovered Duyun; he brought his parents' remains home for burial; he was then only twenty and became known thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanlin reported his father's death to the governor; imperial forces recaptured Duyun, and he brought his parents' remains home for burial. He was only twenty, and his fame dates from that episode.

sentences.zh: 以舉人從欽差大臣勝保徵捻，授同知。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he followed imperial commissioner Sheng Bao in suppressing the Nian and was appointed subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he followed Imperial Commissioner Sheng Bao in the campaign against the Nian and was appointed subprefect.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，成進士，選庶吉士，散館改廣西知縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and after leaving the academy was made a county magistrate in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he earned his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and on completing his academy term was appointed a county magistrate in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 以督剿柳、雒土匪功，賜孔雀翎，擢桂林知府。

translations.literal: For merit in supervising suppression of bandits in Liu and Luo, he was granted a peacock feather and promoted to Guilin prefect.
translations.idiomatic: For supervising the suppression of bandits in Liu and Luo, he was granted a peacock feather and promoted to prefect of Guilin.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，調廉州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he was transferred to Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1878 he was transferred to Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時李揚才將叛擾越南，急捕之，立散其黨。

translations.literal: At the time Li Yangcai was about to rebel and harass Vietnam; he quickly arrested him and immediately dispersed his faction.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Yangcai was plotting rebellion and raids into Vietnam; Lu arrested him at once and broke up his following.

sentences.zh: 旋升惠潮嘉道。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jieyang circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to circuit intendant of Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jieyang.

sentences.zh: 擢福建按察使，調四川，遷布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Fujian provincial judicial commissioner, transferred to Sichuan, and advanced to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Fujian provincial judicial commissioner, transferred to Sichuan, and then made provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 九年，授河南巡撫，清釐州縣納糧積弊，歲增三十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Henan governor, cleared accumulated abuses in prefectural and county grain payments, and increased annual receipts by more than three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In 1883 he was appointed governor of Henan, cleared long-standing abuses in local grain payments, and increased annual revenue by more than three hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 十一年，調陝西，引疾歸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Shaanxi, then cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 he was transferred to Shaanxi, then retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 十五年，再出撫陝。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he went out again to govern Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1889 he returned to govern Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 值黃河西囓，將與洛通。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River was eroding westward and about to join the Luo River,
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River was eroding westward and threatened to join the Luo,

sentences.zh: 傳霖增築石壩三十餘座，得無患。

translations.literal: Chuanlin added more than thirty stone dams and avoided calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Lu built more than thirty stone dams and averted disaster.

sentences.zh: 中日構釁，遣兵入衛，命兼攝西安將軍。

translations.literal: When China and Japan came into conflict he sent troops to guard the capital and was ordered concurrently to act as Xi'an general.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out with Japan he sent troops to guard the court and was ordered to serve concurrently as general at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，擢四川總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to Sichuan governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1895 he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 蜀故多盜，特立一軍捕治之。

translations.literal: Shu had long been full of bandits; he specially established an army to capture and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan had long been plagued by bandits; he formed a special force to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 夔、萬大饑，發上游積穀，又採湖北糧米平糶。

translations.literal: Kui and Wan suffered great famine; he released stored grain from upstream and also procured Hubei grain and rice for sale at fair prices.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui and Wan suffered famine, he released stored grain from upstream and brought in Hubei rice to sell at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 是時英、俄交窺西藏，藏番恃俄援，梗英畫界。

translations.literal: At the time Britain and Russia both eyed Tibet; Tibetan tribes relied on Russian aid and obstructed British boundary demarcation.
translations.idiomatic: Britain and Russia were both watching Tibet; Tibetan tribes relied on Russian support and blocked British boundary demarcation.

sentences.zh: 英嗾廓爾喀與藏構兵，而瞻對土民苦藏官苛虐，思內附。

translations.literal: Britain incited Gurkhas to war with Tibet, while the people of Drayi suffered harsh abuse from Tibetan officials and wished to submit to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Britain incited the Gurkhas to fight Tibet, while the people of Drayi, suffering harsh rule by Tibetan officials, wished to come under Chinese administration.

sentences.zh: 傳霖以瞻對為蜀門戶，瞻不化服，無以威藏番；

translations.literal: Chuanlin held that Drayi was the gateway of Shu; if Drayi were not brought to submission, there would be no means to overawe Tibetan tribes;
translations.idiomatic: Lu held that Drayi was the gateway to Sichuan; unless Drayi submitted, there was no way to intimidate the Tibetan tribes;

sentences.zh: 藏番不聽命，則界無時定。

translations.literal: if Tibetan tribes did not obey orders, the border could never be settled in time.
translations.idiomatic: and if the Tibetan tribes would not obey, the border could never be settled.

sentences.zh: 而英之忌俄者益急圖藏，藏亡瞻必隨亡，行且​​及於蜀。

translations.literal: Those in Britain who feared Russia were ever more urgent in plotting Tibet; if Tibet lost Drayi it would surely follow, and soon Shu would be affected.
translations.idiomatic: British opponents of Russia were pressing ever harder on Tibet; if Tibet lost Drayi it would soon lose everything, and Sichuan would be next.

sentences.zh: 會硃窩、章谷土司爭襲事起，傳霖檄知府羅以禮、知縣穆秉文往諭，以提督周萬順統防邊各軍進駐打箭爐。

translations.literal: When Zhukuo and Zhanggu native chiefs disputed succession, Chuanlin ordered prefect Luo Yili and magistrate Mu Bingwen to go instruct them, and had provincial commander Zhou Wanshun lead border-defense armies to advance and encamp at Dartsendo.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhukuo and Zhanggu chiefs disputed succession, Lu ordered Prefect Luo Yili and Magistrate Mu Bingwen to mediate and had Provincial Commander Zhou Wanshun lead border troops to Dartsendo.

sentences.zh: 瞻酋仔仲則忠札霸以兵侵章谷，抗我軍。

translations.literal: Drayi chieftain Zizhong Zezhong Zhaba invaded Zhanggu with troops and resisted our army.
translations.idiomatic: The Drayi chieftain Zizhong Zezhong Zhaba invaded Zhanggu with troops and resisted the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 傳霖乘機進發，迭克諸要害。

translations.literal: Chuanlin seized the opportunity to advance and captured key points in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Lu seized the opportunity to advance and took key positions one after another.

sentences.zh: 各土司讋服，率兵聽調。

translations.literal: The various native chiefs submitted in fear and led troops to obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: The native chiefs submitted and brought their troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 渡雅龍江抵瞻巢，斬馘過當，盡收三瞻地，乃請歸流改漢，條陳善後之策，疏十數上。

translations.literal: Crossing the Yalong River he reached the Drayi stronghold, beheaded excessively, recovered all the three Drayi regions, then requested conversion to regular administration and sinicization, setting forth postwar policies in more than ten memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yalong River to the Drayi stronghold, executed many captives, recovered all three Drayi districts, and then memorialized repeatedly to place the region under regular administration and sinicize it, setting forth postwar policies in more than ten memorials.

sentences.zh: 會成都將軍恭壽、駐藏辦事大臣文海交章言其不便，達賴复疏訴於朝，廷議中變，傳霖解職去。

translations.literal: When Chengdu general Gongshou and Tibetan resident commissioner Wen Hai jointly memorialized that this was inexpedient, and the Dalai Lama again memorialized in complaint to the court, court deliberation shifted midway and Chuanlin was relieved of office and left.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu General Gongshou and Tibetan Resident Commissioner Wen Hai jointly memorialized that the policy was unwise, and the Dalai Lama appealed to the court; the court reversed course, and Lu was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，召授廣東巡撫，旋移江蘇，攝兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was summoned and appointed Guangdong governor, soon transferred to Jiangsu, and acted as Liangjiang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 he was summoned as governor of Guangdong, soon transferred to Jiangsu, and served as acting governor-general of Liangjiang.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳匪亂作，傳霖募三營入衛，奔及乘輿於大同。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer rebellion broke out; Chuanlin recruited three battalions to enter the guard, and rushed to join the imperial carriage at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, when the Boxer uprising broke out, Lu recruited three battalions to guard the court and caught up with the imperial procession at Datong.

sentences.zh: 至太原，授兩廣總督。

translations.literal: Reaching Taiyuan, he was appointed governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan he was appointed governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 旋命入直軍機，從幸長安。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to enter the Grand Council and followed the court to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered into the Grand Council and accompanied the court to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史，遷禮部尚書，兼署工部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left censor-in-chief, transferred to minister of Rites, and concurrently served as acting minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left censor-in-chief, made minister of Rites, and concurrently served as acting minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明年，回蹕，兼督辦政務大臣。

translations.literal: The next year, when the court returned to the capital, he also supervised administrative reform affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the court returned to Beijing, he also supervised administrative reform.

sentences.zh: 凡疏陳加賦括財、損民以益上者，傳霖率擯勿用；

translations.literal: Whatever memorials proposed increasing taxes, seizing wealth, or harming the people to enrich the throne, Chuanlin generally rejected and would not use them;
translations.idiomatic: He generally rejected memorials proposing tax increases, wealth seizures, or policies that harmed the people to enrich the throne;

sentences.zh: 而務汰冗費，去中飽，並奏罷不急之工：均報可。

translations.literal: but strove to cut redundant expenses, remove middlemen's graft, and also memorialized to stop non-urgent projects: all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: but pressed to cut waste, eliminate graft, and stop nonessential projects, all of which the court approved.

sentences.zh: 有詔自后宮內供需皆取給內務府，戶部專掌軍國大計，實傳霖發之也。

translations.literal: There was an edict that henceforth inner palace supplies should all be drawn from the Imperial Household Department and the Ministry of Revenue should specialize in great state and military plans—this in fact originated with Chuanlin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed that inner palace supplies should come from the Imperial Household Department while the Ministry of Revenue would handle state and military finance—a reform Lu had initiated.

sentences.zh: 三十年，轉吏部。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1904 he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，新官制成，乃退直，專治部事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year the new official system was completed; he then withdrew from council duty and specialized in ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1906, when the new official system took effect, he left the Grand Council to focus on ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋仍入直，解部務，以尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: Before long he again entered the council, relinquished ministry duties, and served as minister with the title associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he reentered the Grand Council, gave up ministry duties, and served as minister and associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 命查辦歸化城墾務大臣貽穀，論遣戍，參劾不職者數十人。

translations.literal: He was ordered to investigate Guihua reclamation commissioner Yigu, who was sentenced to banishment, and impeached dozens of incompetent officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to investigate Guihua reclamation commissioner Yigu, who was sentenced to exile, and impeached dozens of incompetent officials.

sentences.zh: 宣統嗣立，與攝政醇親王同受遺詔，加太子少保，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: When Xuantong succeeded, he and Regent Prince Chun together received the late emperor's testament; he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuantong succeeded, he and Regent Prince Chun received the late emperor's deathbed testament together; he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and then Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 歷拜體仁閣、東閣大學士，兼經筵講官。

translations.literal: He successively served as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence and the Eastern Pavilion, and also lectured at the classics colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence and the Eastern Pavilion and also lectured at the classics colloquium.

sentences.zh: 二年春，疾作，章四上，皆溫諭慰留。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year illness set in; he memorialized four times, and each time received warm edicts urging him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1910 he fell ill and submitted four retirement memorials; each time the court warmly urged him to remain.

sentences.zh: 七月，卒，年七十五，贈太保，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he died at age seventy-five, was posthumously granted Grand Guardian, and given the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month at the age of seventy-five and was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 傳霖起外吏，知民疾苦。

translations.literal: Chuanlin rose from local officialdom and knew the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Lu rose from local officialdom and knew the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 所至廉約率下，尤惡貪吏，雖貴勢不稍貰。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he was frugal and restrained subordinates, especially hating corrupt officials, and would not spare even the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he was frugal and restrained his subordinates, hated corrupt officials above all, and would not spare even the powerful.

sentences.zh: 其在軍機，凡事不苟同，喜扶持善類。

translations.literal: In the Grand Council he never agreed casually on affairs and liked to support worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: In the Grand Council he never agreed casually and liked to support worthy men.

sentences.zh: 晚病重聽，屢乞休不獲，居恆鬱鬱雲。

translations.literal: In his later years his illness made him hard of hearing; he repeatedly begged to retire without success and lived in constant gloom.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years illness left him hard of hearing; he repeatedly asked to retire without success and lived in gloom.

sentences.zh: 林紹年，字贊虞，福建閩縣人。

translations.literal: Lin Shaonian, style name Zanyu, was a native of Min county in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shaonian, whose style was Zanyu, came from Min county in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 同治十三年進士，以編修歷充鄉會試同考官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Tongzhi and as a compiler served repeatedly as associate examiner for provincial and metropolitan examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1874 and as a Hanlin compiler served repeatedly as associate examiner for provincial and metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 光緒十四年，改御史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Guangxu he was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1888 he was made a censor.

sentences.zh: 時議修頤和園，先是疆吏籌​​設海軍經費，輸存北洋，及園工興，陰移其費以助工，號為「進獻」。

translations.literal: At the time restoration of the Summer Palace was under discussion; earlier frontier governors had raised naval funds and deposited them with the Beiyang fleet, but when palace work began they secretly diverted the funds to aid construction, calling it "tribute offerings."
translations.idiomatic: The court was discussing restoration of the Summer Palace; frontier governors had earlier raised naval funds and deposited them with the Beiyang fleet, but when palace construction began they secretly diverted the money and called it "tribute offerings."

sentences.zh: 紹年極陳：「生民疲敝，當以儉化天下，使督撫愛養百姓。

translations.literal: Shaonian strongly stated: "The people are exhausted; the realm should be transformed by thrift, and governors and governors-general should cherish and nurture the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Lin protested forcefully: "The people are exhausted; the court should lead the realm by example in thrift and require governors to care for the people.

sentences.zh: 若誅求進獻，未足以言忠。

translations.literal: If they extort tribute offerings, that is not enough to be called loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Extorting such offerings is not loyalty.

sentences.zh: 請即下詔停輸，還所進奉。

translations.literal: I beg that an edict immediately stop the payments and return what has been offered.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the court immediately order the payments stopped and the offerings returned.

sentences.zh: 」得旨嚴飭。

translations.literal: " He received an edict sternly rebuking the practice.
translations.idiomatic: " The court issued a stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 會以憂去，服除，補山西監察御史。

translations.literal: He then went out on mourning, and after mourning ended was appointed Shanxi surveillance censor.
translations.idiomatic: He then went on mourning leave, and on returning was appointed surveillance censor in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 疏嚴門禁，杜宦寺交通之漸。

translations.literal: He memorialized to tighten palace gates and cut off the tendency of eunuchs to form outside connections.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to tighten palace security and block eunuchs from forming outside connections.

sentences.zh: 十九年，陝西考官丁維禔夤緣內監得試差，复疏論之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Shaanxi examiner Ding Weiti obtained an examination assignment through connections with inner eunuchs; he again memorialized criticizing this.
translations.idiomatic: In 1893, when Shaanxi examiner Ding Weiti obtained his assignment through eunuch connections, Lin memorialized against the practice again.

sentences.zh: 俄，授雲南昭通府知府。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed prefect of Zhaotong in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed prefect of Zhaotong in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 邊瘠難治，土目祿爾泰橫暴，睚眥殺人，莫敢訴，猝捕戮之，眾懾而定。

translations.literal: The border was poor and hard to govern; native chieftain Lu Ertai was violent, killing over trifles; none dared accuse him; Lin suddenly arrested and executed him, and the crowd submitted in fear and order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The border was poor and hard to govern; native chieftain Lu Ertai was violent and killed over trifles with impunity. Lin arrested and executed him at once, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 期年劾罷文武吏不職者五人。

translations.literal: Within a year he impeached and dismissed five incompetent civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he impeached and dismissed five incompetent civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 調攝雲南府，甫受事，安寧州盜劫貨戕人於塗，州牧以總督崧蕃怒緝捕不力，妄系平民二十餘。

translations.literal: Transferred to act as Yunnan prefect, as soon as he took office bandits in Anning robbed goods and killed people on the road; the prefect, because Governor Songfan was angry at ineffective pursuit, wrongly detained more than twenty civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to act as prefect of Yunnan, he had barely taken office when bandits in Anning robbed and killed travelers on the road; the local prefect, fearing Governor Songfan's anger over poor policing, wrongly detained more than twenty civilians.

sentences.zh: 紹年覆按，疑其枉，謁總督廷爭，卒獲正犯，出二十餘人者於死。

translations.literal: Shaonian reinvestigated, suspected wrongful conviction, called on the governor and argued in court, at last obtained the real culprits, and released the more than twenty from death.
translations.idiomatic: Lin reinvestigated, suspected a miscarriage of justice, went to the governor and argued the case in court, eventually found the real culprits, and saved more than twenty innocent men from execution.

sentences.zh: 崧蕃愧謝，密疏薦紹年可大用。

translations.literal: Songfan apologized in shame and secretly memorialized recommending Shaonian for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: Songfan apologized and secretly recommended Lin for higher office.

sentences.zh: 擢迤南道，未之任，擢貴州按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Yinan circuit intendant, did not take the post, and was promoted to Guizhou provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to circuit intendant of Yinan but did not take the post and was made Guizhou provincial judicial commissioner instead.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，遷雲南布政使，就擢巡撫，兼署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to Yunnan provincial treasurer, then promoted to governor and concurrently acted as Yun-Gui governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 he was transferred to Yunnan provincial treasurer, then promoted to governor and concurrently served as acting governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 廣西遊匪侵滇邊，遣將擊卻之。

translations.literal: Guangxi roaming bandits invaded the Yunnan border; he sent generals to attack and drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangxi roaming bandits raided the Yunnan border, he sent generals to drive them back.

sentences.zh: 招撫八達河村民之陷匪者，以斷賊接濟，益大出兵合剿。

translations.literal: He pacified Badu River villagers who had joined the bandits, to cut off rebel supplies, and further sent large forces for joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified villagers along the Badu River who had joined the bandits, cutting off rebel supplies, and then sent larger forces for a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 滇境既清，乃以全力赴援廣西，而蒙自土匪乘間復發，連陷臨安、石屏。

translations.literal: Once Yunnan was pacified he devoted full strength to aiding Guangxi, but Mengzi bandits seized the interval to rise again and successively captured Lin'an and Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yunnan was pacified he sent full aid to Guangxi, but Mengzi bandits seized the chance to rise again and took Lin'an and Shiping in succession.

sentences.zh: 紹年會商總督丁振鐸，檄按察使劉春霖扼通海，廣南軍躡其後，不兩月事平。

translations.literal: Shaonian consulted Governor Ding Zhenduo, ordered provincial judicial commissioner Liu Chunlin to hold Tonghai, and Guangnan troops followed in their rear; within two months affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lin consulted Governor Ding Zhenduo, ordered Provincial Judicial Commissioner Liu Chunlin to hold Tonghai while Guangnan troops pursued from behind, and within two months the rebellion was suppressed.

sentences.zh: 疏言督撫同城任事非便，自請裁缺，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that governor and governor-general in the same city was inconvenient for conducting affairs, begged to abolish the redundant post, and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that having governor and governor-general in the same city was awkward, asked to abolish the redundant post, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 移撫貴州，而湖北、廣東兩巡撫旋亦議裁。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Guizhou, and soon the Hubei and Guangdong governorships were also discussed for abolition.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guizhou, and soon the governorships of Hubei and Guangdong were also slated for abolition.

sentences.zh: 印江團首呂志禮、楊鑫不相能，積十餘載，相殘殺。

translations.literal: Yinjiang militia leaders Lü Zhili and Yang Xin were incompatible; for more than ten years they slaughtered each other.
translations.idiomatic: Yinjiang militia leaders Lü Zhili and Yang Xin had been feuding for more than ten years and killing each other.

sentences.zh: 紹年至，以兵脅之降，仍擁眾不散，遂案誅之。

translations.literal: When Shaonian arrived he threatened them with troops to submit; they still held crowds without dispersing, so he prosecuted and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin arrived he threatened them with troops to submit; they still kept their forces together, so he prosecuted and executed them.

sentences.zh: 紹年默察大勢，非立憲不足以救亡，請預定政體以係人心，不報。

translations.literal: Shaonian silently observed the great trend: without constitutionalism the state could not be saved; he requested fixing the political system in advance to bind popular hearts, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Lin saw clearly that only constitutional government could save the dynasty and asked that the political system be fixed in advance to steady public opinion, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，移廣西。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1905 he was transferred to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，內召，以侍郎充軍機大臣，兼署郵傳部尚書，授度支部侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned to the capital, served as vice minister in the Grand Council, concurrently acted as minister of Posts and Communications, and was appointed vice minister of the Treasury Board.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned to the capital, served as vice minister on the Grand Council, concurrently headed the Ministry of Posts and Communications, and was appointed vice minister of the Treasury Board.

sentences.zh: 時黑龍江新設行省，驟擢道員段芝貴為巡撫。

translations.literal: At the time Heilongjiang was newly made a province and circuit intendant Duan Zhigui was abruptly promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: Heilongjiang had just been made a province, and Circuit Intendant Duan Zhigui was abruptly promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 紹年言芝貴望輕，不稱邊帥任。

translations.literal: Shaonian said Zhigui's standing was light and he did not fit the border commander post.
translations.idiomatic: Lin said Duan's reputation was too slight for a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 御史趙啟霖劾芝貴，因及慶親王奕劻子載振納賄漁色事，命大臣按驗所劾，稱無左證，褫啟霖職，而芝貴亦由是罷。

translations.literal: Censor Zhao Qilin impeached Zhigui and also involved Prince Qing Yikuang's son Zaizhen in taking bribes and pursuing women; grandees were ordered to verify the charges, declared there was no corroboration, stripped Qilin of office, but Zhigui was also dismissed thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Qilin impeached Duan and also accused Prince Qing Yikuang's son Zaizhen of bribery and debauchery; grandees were ordered to investigate, found no proof, and stripped Zhao of office, but Duan was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 紹年言御史風聞言事，啟霖無罪，爭之不得，遂稱疾。

translations.literal: Shaonian said censors report on hearsay and Qilin was innocent; he argued without success and then claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: Lin argued that censors were meant to report on hearsay and that Zhao was innocent; when he failed to prevail he claimed illness.

sentences.zh: 出為河南巡撫。

translations.literal: He went out as Henan governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 以州縣吏罄貲遠宦，人地不習，無益於杜弊。

translations.literal: Because prefectural and county officials exhausted their wealth to serve far from home, were unfamiliar with people and land, and this did no good for stopping abuses,
translations.idiomatic: Because county officials often exhausted their fortunes to serve far from home and knew neither the people nor the locality, which did nothing to stop corruption,

sentences.zh: 請援漢、唐故事，免避本籍。

translations.literal: he requested following Han and Tang precedents to exempt avoidance of one's home province.
translations.idiomatic: he asked to follow Han and Tang precedent and exempt lower officials from the rule barring service in one's home province.

sentences.zh: 部議自縣丞以下，如所請行。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and from assistant magistrate downward approved as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved his request for all posts from assistant magistrate downward.

sentences.zh: 益飭吏治，得朝貴請託書輒焚之。

translations.literal: He further tightened official discipline; whenever he received letters of request from court nobles he burned them.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened official discipline further and burned any letters of recommendation from court nobles.

sentences.zh: 兩疏糾彈百餘人。

translations.literal: In two memorials he impeached more than a hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: In two memorials he impeached more than a hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 調倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the granary depots.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of the granary depots.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，徙民政部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he was transferred to vice minister of Civil Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1909 he was transferred to vice minister of Civil Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時奕劻握政柄，陝西巡撫恩壽與有連，總督升允劾其贓私，不報。

translations.literal: At the time Yikuang held political power; Shaanxi governor Enshou was connected with him; governor-general Sheng Yun impeached his corruption and private conduct, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qing Yikuang then held power; Shaanxi Governor Enshou was connected with him; Governor-General Sheng Yun impeached Enshou for corruption, but the court took no action.

sentences.zh: 俄，解升允職。

translations.literal: Before long Sheng Yun was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sheng Yun was dismissed instead.

sentences.zh: 紹年召對論其事，以為賞罰不當，則是非不明。

translations.literal: Shaonian was summoned for audience to discuss the matter and held that if rewards and punishments were improper, right and wrong would be unclear.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was summoned to discuss the matter and argued that when rewards and punishments were misapplied, right and wrong became impossible to discern.

sentences.zh: 退复具疏言之，不省。

translations.literal: After retiring he again set forth the matter in a memorial; it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving audience he memorialized again on the point, but the court paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 二年，充經筵講官，署學部侍郎，改弼德院顧問大臣。

translations.literal: In the second year he served as classics colloquium lecturer, acted as vice minister of Education, and was changed to advisory grandee of the Bide Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1910 he served as classics colloquium lecturer, acted as vice minister of Education, and was made advisory grandee of the Bide Academy.

sentences.zh: 以病請告。

translations.literal: He requested leave on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested sick leave.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八，諡文直。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-eight and was given the posthumous name Wenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight and was given the posthumous name Wenzhi.

sentences.zh: 論曰：同、光以後，世稱軍機權重，然特領班王大臣主其事耳。

translations.literal: The commentary says: After Tongzhi and Guangxu, the age called the Grand Council's power weighty, yet in fact only the leading prince grandee directed its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: After the Tongzhi and Guangxu reigns, the Grand Council was said to wield great power, but in fact only the leading prince grandee truly directed its affairs.

sentences.zh: 次者僅乃得參機務。

translations.literal: Those below him merely gained participation in state secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Those beneath him could only take part in deliberations.

sentences.zh: 光、宣之際，政既失馭，權乃益紛，雖當國無以為治焉。

translations.literal: Between Guangxu and Xuantong, government had already lost control, power grew ever more fragmented, and even those who held the state could not govern it.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Guangxu and Xuantong reigns, government had lost its grip, power grew ever more fragmented, and even those nominally in charge could no longer govern effectively.

sentences.zh: 敬銘質樸，之萬練達，傳霖廉約，紹年勁直，其任封疆、治軍旅多有績，而立朝不復有所建樹。

translations.literal: Jingming was plain, Zhiwan experienced, Chuanlin frugal, Shaonian firm and upright; in frontier posts and military affairs they had many achievements, but at court they no longer had notable accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was plain, Zhang experienced, Lu frugal, and Lin firm and upright; all achieved much on the frontier and in military affairs, but at court they accomplished little.

sentences.zh: 敬銘初欲得君專國政，為勢所限，終不能行其志，世尤惜之。

translations.literal: Jingming at first wished to win the ruler and monopolize state affairs, but was constrained by circumstances and in the end could not carry out his will; the age especially regretted this.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had once hoped to win the emperor's trust and direct state policy, but circumstances blocked him and he never realized his aims—a loss the age especially regretted.
